key_insight: AI-based tumour-infiltrating lymphocyte scoring (TRIGS and SAM-TIL) predicted treatment response and survival in triple negative breast cancer about as well as gold-standard clinical scoring.
clinical_relevance: These tools could help standardize TIL assessment for prognosis in neoadjuvant and early-stage breast cancer research, but they are not yet a replacement for pathologist review.
method: Updated an automated TIL pipeline to match clinical scoring guidance (TRIGS).
Used a foundation model for lymphocyte detection (SAM-TIL) and compared it with HoVerNet and muTILs.
Benchmarked models against gold-standard clinical assessment and outcomes across multiple cohorts.
evidence_signal: In the PARTNER and external cohorts, the models showed moderate correlation with clinical scoring (0.59-0.69) and similar prognostic performance for pCR and event-free survival, with pCR AUC around 0.60-0.64 and comparable Brier scores.
watch_item: Model detections were not interchangeable with manual clinical scoring, so independent validation and careful implementation are needed before routine use.
paper_title: Tumour region identification guided scoring (TRIGS) and foundation model-based Tumour Infiltrating Lymphocyte scoring are prognostic for pathological complete response/event free survival in the triple negative patients in the PARTNER randomized controlled trial
